corrections.title: Guardini's higher humility
corrections.what: The fear that Christ's divinity makes him distant is backwards: only as true God is Jesus our contemporary. The higher humility lets God do what seems unfitting — bow down to us.
corrections.quote: the higher form of humility consists in allowing God to do precisely what appears to us to be unfitting

corrections.title: No divinizing of the world
corrections.what: He heads off the pantheist misreading of the Trinity chapter: the world is created by the personal logos and is good — it shares the divine as gift, never as identity.
corrections.quote: The world comes from reason, and this reason is a Person, is Love

corrections.title: The God with nothing to do
corrections.what: The deeper problem is not militant atheism but the privatized God of a faith lived etsi Deus non daretur: when faith went public it left God unemployed in the private sphere.
corrections.quote: to leave God as a God with nothing to do

corrections.title: 1968 and 1989 milestones
corrections.what: 1989 refutes Marxism's ethical promise — the guide to the future collapsed into ruined land and ruined souls — yet Christianity still failed to sound as the epoch-making alternative.
corrections.quote: a sorry legacy of ruined land and ruined souls

corrections.title: Reception and reprint policy
corrections.what: The book found unexpected readers across the East-West boundary and denominations; technical criticisms were answered elsewhere, and the 1969 reprint keeps the text unaltered apart from minor errors.
corrections.quote: The book itself is being reprinted with the text unaltered; just a few minor errors have been corrected.

corrections.title: Gold traded for a whetstone
corrections.what: The book refuses both errors of its moment: theology's stepwise watering-down of faith (gold traded to a whetstone) and mere restoration, which leaves the old formulas a dead lump of metal.
corrections.quote: merely sticking to the precious metal of the fixed formulas of days gone by

corrections.title: What he would rewrite
corrections.what: Thirty years on he would widen the interreligious context, but not the architecture: God and Christ at the center, narrative Christology, faith's place in the Church — the basic approach stands.
corrections.quote: I believe that I was not mistaken as to the fundamental approach

scripture.text: Moses asks God's name; God answers "I am who I am" — the God of the fathers.
scripture.ratzinger: Calls the burning bush the central Old Testament text on God: the revelation of the name to Moses lays the foundation for Israel's idea of God, the thread for all that follows.

scripture.text: God's answer "I am" — a refusal of name that dissolves into mystery, yet promises "I am here for you".
scripture.ratzinger: He reads the name both ways at once: gesture of repulse that "dissolves the name into mystery", and promise — "I am" means "I am here for you", God's being is Being-for.

scripture.text: The eternal Word through whom all things were made became flesh — John's logos hymn.
scripture.ratzinger: Ever since John's Prologue logos stands at Christianity's center: meaning that is Word, relationship, creative reason — guaranteeing the world's intelligibility and its goodness.

scripture.text: "Let us make man" — the plural in which the Fathers found a "We" in God.
scripture.ratzinger: Scripture's grammar supplies the Trinity: in God dialogue, an "I" and "You". This forces the concept person — relation gains a new dignity beside substance.

scripture.text: "I have manifested your name to the men whom you gave me out of the world"
scripture.ratzinger: John 17 is the New Testament counterpart to the burning bush: Christ is the burning bush from which God's name issues; made known, that name draws believers into the love of Father and Son.

scripture.text: Christ empties himself, taking the form of a servant, obedient to death on a cross.
scripture.ratzinger: The hymn's fullest statement of son-as-servant: exinanivit — he "emptied" himself, surrendering existence-for-self into pure "for"; there the servant becomes the true ruler, lord of the cosmos.

scripture.text: "You are my son, today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will make the nations your heritage."
scripture.ratzinger: The coronation oracle explains Cross and Resurrection: Son of God is Israel's royal theology of election and hope — kingship as standing for others — never Hellenistic myth.

scripture.text: The Good Shepherd says he is the door: whoever enters through him is saved.
scripture.ratzinger: From the Good Shepherd discourse: Christ is the door between God and man — in him the Eternal One has time for the world, so the ascended Lord is near.

scripture.text: Death and Hades thrown into the lake of fire — the "second death".
scripture.ratzinger: Since love now dwells in death, death itself is no longer hell; only deliberate self-enclosure — the second death — is. The descent redefines hell anthropologically.

scripture.text: The shepherd searches for the one lost sheep; heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents.
scripture.ratzinger: Uses the lost sheep and drachma to transform the philosophical God: the Bible's God seeks, loves, and rejoices — the question of who God is is asked and answered here.
